A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MS-IMAP. All 29 pages of v4 and 31 pages of v5, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison. Relocated content and renumbered theoretical results can be matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original clustering experiments, feature-selection evaluations, hyperparameter ablations, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds scattering-baseline comparisons and HAR/AwA feature-selection evaluations.

M1.justification: The SGW encoding, tensor construction, cross-entropy objective, joint SGD updates, scale summation, and LS/MI feature-selection procedures are retained. v5 expands explanations of coordinate updates and scale energy without specifying a different algorithm or loss.

E1.justification: The same six datasets remain. Feature-selection evaluation extends from Cora and Zilionis to HAR and AwA, previously evaluated through full-embedding clustering. This broadens coverage of the feature-selection application without introducing new datasets.

E2.justification: v5 adds scattering comparisons in Tables 1–2, labeled Scattering.T and Scattering Geometric.T. Diffusion Maps, renamed DM in Table 1, gains reported HAR results and loses its numerical Zilionis comparison. The remaining comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: Table 4 expands the t-SNE perplexity search from 15, 30, and 60 to include 200, with corresponding evaluation in Table 9. Other listed search grids and the k-means, ARI, and AMI evaluation framework remain unchanged. This establishes a reported protocol revision, not necessarily that previous experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 extends the existing feature-subset analysis to HAR and AwA in Figures 5–6 and the t-SNE sensitivity analysis to perplexity 200. It removes v4's Diffusion Maps kernel-width analysis and Table 11. The Cora/Zilionis analyses are retained and redisplayed.

E5.justification: v4 provides point estimates in Table 1; v5 reports means and standard deviations throughout this central comparison, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. The five-runs-per-configuration statement for tuned baselines is retained in Appendix 8.5; an increased run count or new significance testing is not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises several baseline means: t-SNE HAR ARI/AMI changes from 0.71/0.77 to 0.62/0.70, and UMAP Zilionis AMI from 0.74 to 0.71. MS-IMAP's means remain unchanged. v5 adds scattering results, HAR/AwA feature-subset curves, and perplexity-200 results; Tables 7–8 correct Census ARI from 0.22 to 0.23. The Diffusion Maps sensitivity results and concatenation method's 12.44-minute Cancer QC runtime disappear. The changed t-SNE search prevents treating its replacements as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The Paley-Wiener definitions, sampling results, lemmas, proofs, and coefficient derivations match across versions. The theoretical section moves from Section 4 to Section 6, and appendix theorems are renumbered, without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: multiscale SGW contrastive embeddings, explicit feature correspondence for interpretation, and theoretical advantages over the Laplacian representation. Competitive clustering remains a core claim. v5 foregrounds interpretability while retaining these claims' scope.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 explains how LS can favor smoothly varying but uninformative features and contrasts this with MI's clustering relevance and noise behavior. v5 also discusses ambient-dimensional embeddings and compatibility with alternative wavelet representations. Pseudo-label dependence and the main out-of-sample, manifold-quality, and local-importance limitations were already present.

D1.justification: v5 explicitly identifies the adaptive graph kernel adopted from reference 25, previously presented as an option, and expands coordinate-update documentation. It removes the separate concatenation-method Cancer QC runtime and the 5,685-sample AwA runtime specification. Hardware and the other reported runtime values are retained.

R1.justification: All 40 references match. However, Section 2 expands discussion of high-dimensional embedding limitations and computational costs, while Section 5.2 positions MS-IMAP against graph scattering as an additional high-dimensional comparator. This revises positioning without expanding the bibliography.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, preliminaries, feature-importance discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Feature importance moves ahead of experiments, theory moves after them, LS versus MI receives a dedicated subsection, and the appendix is reorganized under Section 8.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 8 to page 2. Four existing Cora/Zilionis plots are regrouped into paired main-text Figures 2–3, and new HAR/AwA panels form Figures 5–6. Table 1 is reformatted for means and standard deviations, Table 9 gains a row, and the Diffusion Maps sensitivity table is removed.

improvement.justification: v5 broadens empirical support for feature importance through HAR/AwA evaluations and makes the main comparison more informative through a scattering baseline and standard deviations. The reorganized explanation also helps readers assess the interpretability contribution. These gains outweigh the limited loss of supplementary sensitivity and runtime evidence, although unexplained baseline-score replacements and an unresolved figure reference limit the improvement.
